extracted.intended_audience: members of the public/citizens who want to comment or participate in NEPA reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for citizens on how and when to participate in the NEPA process, including scoping and comment periods for Environmental Impact Statements and practical advice for writing effective comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key participation opportunities / timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Two primary moments for public involvement: "When an agency begins the NEPA analysis" and "When a NEPA document is published for public review and comment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate early during scoping to help shape the scope and priorities of the review, and again when draft NEPA documents (e.g., Draft EIS) are published. Monitor Federal Register notices, agency websites, and newspaper notices for announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency notification methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies use varied notification methods, including Federal Register publications, agency websites, and newspaper notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check multiple sources (Federal Register, agency project pages, local newspapers) to learn about notices of intent, scoping opportunities, and publication of draft documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping process / Notice of Intent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When an Environmental Impact Statement is required, agencies publish a Notice of Intent in the Federal Register, initiating scoping and describing "the proposed action and a description of the scoping process, including any scheduled meetings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping is the opportunity to shape environmental review priorities and the range of issues and alternatives to be analyzed. Look for Notice of Intent details to know how and when to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement formats available
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies employ multiple engagement formats: public meetings, conference calls, formal hearings, informal workshops, written comment opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the format that best suits your ability to present information—written comments for detailed evidence, meetings/hearings for verbal input and to raise issues publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft EIS comment period length and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft Environmental Impact Statements remain open for public feedback for "a minimum of 45 days."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note and observe comment deadlines—use the Active EIS Database or Federal Register notices to find exact deadlines for each project and plan time to prepare substantive comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens can submit comments via email or attend in-person meetings to voice concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the contact and submission instructions provided in the notice or on the agency/project page; keep copies of submitted comments and any supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, concision, and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be "clear, concise, and relevant" to the analysis of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus comments on issues the agency can analyze in the NEPA document. Avoid long, unfocused narratives; use headings or bullet points to make key points easy for reviewers to find.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be solutions-oriented and provide specific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that are "solutions-oriented", provide "specific examples", and contribute to developing alternatives will be more effective than those that simply convey opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose concrete mitigation measures or alternative approaches, cite studies or local data, and explain how suggested alternatives would reduce environmental impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate claims of significance with causes and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: General comments that state an action will have "significant environmental effects" will not help an agency make a better decision unless the comment explains the relevant causes and environmental effects and why the issues raised are significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting significance, explain causal links (what action causes what effect), provide evidence or examples, and explain why the effect is important in the context of the project area or resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EPA Active EIS Database to find project details
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA maintains an online database of active Environmental Impact Statements, displaying: project names, lead agencies, locations, comment deadlines, contact information for each proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the database to identify projects, verify deadlines and contacts, and obtain basic project metadata before preparing comments or planning participation.
